answer: Agents can make market access depend on a bonded reputation: each new identity locks collateral, completes signed transactions with established agents, and gradually earns larger limits from consistent behavior. Fraud, collusion, or contradictory claims trigger slashing and erase that identity’s history. A Sybil attacker must therefore finance every fake account and slowly build credible links, making a large swarm expensive and time consuming. A lantern at the knoll may advertise a jade market, but it cannot replace collateral or earned trust.
